question_vi: Build artifact, immutable image, semantic versioning trong CI/CD?
question_en: Build artifacts, immutable images, and semantic versioning in CI/CD?
answer_vi: Build once, deploy many: artifact (Docker image, jar, zip) build 1 lần ở stage CI, promote qua các môi trường (dev → staging → prod) — không bao giờ rebuild từ source ở mỗi môi trường. **Tại sao immutable**: rebuild ở mỗi env risk subtle drift (npm install cùng `package.json` nhưng khác lockfile resolution, base image bị cập nhật mà không ai hay). Image tag bằng commit SHA hoặc semver, không bao giờ overwrite `latest` cho production. **Semantic versioning (semver)**: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` — MAJOR khi breaking, MINOR cho feature mới backward-compat, PATCH cho bug fix. Pre-release: `1.2.0-rc.1`, `2.0.0-beta.3`. Automated tooling: `semantic-release` (commit message convention `feat:`, `fix:`, `BREAKING CHANGE:` → tự bump version + tạo changelog + tag Git + publish npm). **Container image tag strategy**: 3 tag cùng lúc — `myapp:1.4.2` (semver), `myapp:1.4.2-a3f8c9` (semver + commit SHA cho traceability), `myapp:latest` (chỉ cho dev/staging, không prod). **Artifact registry**: GitHub Container Registry, AWS ECR, Google Artifact Registry — lưu image với retention policy (xoá image > 30 ngày trừ tagged release). **SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)**: generate khi build (`syft` hoặc `cosign`), lưu cùng artifact để audit compliance và detect vulnerable dependency sau publish
answer_en: Build once, deploy many: an artifact (Docker image, jar, zip) is built once in the CI stage and promoted through environments (dev → staging → prod) — never rebuilt from source per environment. **Why immutable**: rebuilding in each environment risks subtle drift (npm install with the same `package.json` but different lockfile resolution, base image silently updated). Tag images by commit SHA or semver, never overwrite `latest` for production. **Semantic versioning (semver)**: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` — bump MAJOR on breaking changes, MINOR for backward-compatible features, PATCH for bug fixes. Pre-releases: `1.2.0-rc.1`, `2.0.0-beta.3`. Automated tooling: `semantic-release` (commit message conventions `feat:`, `fix:`, `BREAKING CHANGE:` → auto-bumps the version, generates the changelog, tags Git, publishes to npm). **Container image tag strategy**: three tags applied simultaneously — `myapp:1.4.2` (semver), `myapp:1.4.2-a3f8c9` (semver + commit SHA for traceability), `myapp:latest` (dev/staging only, never production). **Artifact registry**: GitHub Container Registry, AWS ECR, Google Artifact Registry — store images with a retention policy (delete images >30 days except tagged releases). **SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)**: generate at build time (`syft` or `cosign`), store alongside the artifact for compliance auditing and post-publish vulnerability detection

Build once, deploy many: an artifact (Docker image, jar, zip) is built once in the CI stage and promoted through environments (dev → staging → prod) — never rebuilt from source per environment. Why immutable: rebuilding in each environment risks subtle drift (npm install with the same package.json but different lockfile resolution, base image silently updated).

  • Tag images by commit SHA or semver, never overwrite latest for production. Semantic versioning (semver): MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH — bump MAJOR on breaking changes, MINOR for backward-compatible features, PATCH for bug fixes.
  • Pre-releases: 1.2.0-rc.1, 2.0.0-beta.3.
  • Automated tooling: semantic-release (commit message conventions feat:, fix:, BREAKING CHANGE: → auto-bumps the version, generates the changelog, tags Git, publishes to npm). Container image tag strategy: three tags applied simultaneously — myapp:1.4.2 (semver), myapp:1.4.2-a3f8c9 (semver + commit SHA for traceability), myapp:latest (dev/staging only, never production). Artifact registry: GitHub Container Registry, AWS ECR, Google Artifact Registry — store images with a retention policy (delete images >30 days except tagged releases). SBOM (Software Bill of Materials): generate at build time (syft or cosign), store alongside the artifact for compliance auditing and post-publish vulnerability detection.
